content:
When adding verso integration to Formal Conjectures (FC#3585) the question came up if it'd be better to put the verso dependency in a separate lakefile or in the separate project or just in the main lakefile of the project, see here
What is the recommended way of adding verso (we are basically only using verso-literate for now)?
It looks quite nice, and was fairly easy to set up, btw, thanks for the good work!
and also builds much faster on our fairly large repo than docgen

My personal take: Putting verso in a separate lakefile serves a couple of purposes:

  • Allows (some) contributors to work on the project without having to care about the Verso-generated documentation locally
  • Prevents version clashes between dependencies of Verso and your own.

I think in particular the first point was very useful in the context of #Analysis I (where we have the separated setup)

In the context of Waterproof we're using Verso as a direct dependency in our Genre, but there the Verso functionality is core to our fileformat.

I suspect Formal Conjectures is closer to the former than the latter.

Glad you're seeing benefit there!

I've actually got a setup for projects like #Analysis I that won't require a version separation almost finished. It does mean version-locking, but it should be pretty stable over time and not impose big difficulties. I'll post about it here when it's done.
